note: Leuven second town wall (built 1357-63, still standing in 1650), traced from the Ferraris map (1777). Local metres around the Grote Markt (x east, z south). Gate names: Dutch for the Ferraris labels.

gateSources.Mechelsepoort: Ferraris 'Pte de Malines'; name confirmed by inventory 140040 (Historische stadskern van Leuven)
gateSources.Aarschotsepoort: Ferraris 'Pte d'Aerschot ou ...' (second name illegible); name confirmed by inventory 140040 (Historische stadskern van Leuven)
gateSources.Diestsepoort: Ferraris 'Pte de Diest'; name confirmed by inventory 140040 (Historische stadskern van Leuven)
gateSources.Tiensepoort: Ferraris 'Pte de Tirlemont'; name confirmed by inventory 140040 (Historische stadskern van Leuven)
gateSources.Parkpoort: Ferraris 'Pte de Parc'; name confirmed by inventory 140040 (Historische stadskern van Leuven)
gateSources.Naamsepoort: Ferraris 'Pte de Namur ou Heverlé'; name confirmed by inventory 140040 (Historische stadskern van Leuven)
gateSources.Oude Brusselsepoort: inventory 140040 lists the 8 gates of the second wall incl. the 'Oude Brusselsepoort'; Ferraris 'Vieille Pte de Bruxelles ou du Chateau' (was 'Tervuursepoort' in the first version, a later name)
gateSources.Wijngaardpoort: inventory 140040 ('Wijngaardpoort'); Ferraris 'Pte de Bruxelles ou des Vignes' (was 'Brusselsepoort', the 18th-c. name)

source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Leuven' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140040)
